While No Mans Sky is a skinners Box in many regards, it has a lot of elements that keep it engaging. Sure you can boil down it's progression into collecting things, to make it easier to collect more things, but the game is best enjoyed if you're ok with letting your imagination do most of the heavy lifting. I'd compare this game more to Daggerfall. than Minecraft, or Subnautica, as this game has a sense of freedom unprecedented in other survival crafting games. Want to build a base and gradually work your way up through the ranks solely on whats available to you on the starting planet? You can do that, Want to gain the system by exploiting the economy and finding viable trade routes that lead to more profits mostly sticking to space exploration and commerce, thats doable too. Basically mostly anything you come up with as a way to get by in this game is possible leading to the ability to specialize which gives this game more depth than you'd think. Even if you didnt feel like specializing the sheer plethora of things you can do in this game allow you to do a mix of everything and still find a fun playstyle in it. A few problems I have with this game is the repetitiveness of the planets as they're all built on the same foundational base but reskinned. This doesn't mean exploration is pointless, just that your imagination is going to be doing most of the work. Another issue I have is how easy survival difficulty can be. Most space combat encounters I've had so far (40 hours in) consists of holding the S key shooting shields until they go down and then following up with a rocket. I wish the combat felt a bit more engaging and like you were actually piloting a ship but I understand thats a big ask for a game balancing multiple systems the way it does. It also disincentivizes any need to upgrade your ship as upgrades will only make it easier to get through combat encounters. I'm not sure if this game contains "post game" content like end game raids or boss fights, and stronger encounters but I feel it'd greatly benefit from one as it would give you something to use all your high tier gear and items on. Rather than purely using it for efficiency and base building. The tutorial is by the worst part of the game I understand it's use and purpose but I don't agree with how it was handled. I'd rather the game allow me to figure out it's systems naturally than force me to follow the first quarter of a tutorial in order to gain the ability to create essential structures and items TLDR; if you like games like Daggerfall or Dwarf Fortress you'll probably like this game

No Man's Sky has consumed me. It is a great and terrible slow burn, which over the years has taken me from struggle to a feeling of omnipotence, from obsessive multi-day binge plays to months without picking it up to logging on seven times a day to manage a little town on a planet I didn't like as much as I thought I would. There is so much to do, and yet so little to do if you search with the wrong hunger. I struggled to really enjoy the game after the first two dozen hours. It felt aimless. But new expeditions and updates kept calling me back, and I started to see the light. There is so much to do if you stop looking for gameplay incentives and rewards. Sure, you can optimize your starship and freighter and production and weaponry to be an immortal, but why not just pick a galaxy and spend a day core-to-core jumping to get there? See what it's like? You can find a perfect Earthlike planet if you really try, but why not see the variety of planets that are out there and just... wander? Build a pretty house somewhere. Go fishing! Read the changelogs and additions and just spend some time going around your local stellar neighborhood to find all the things! Write a little story inspired by things you find. Read the amazing story left to grow by the developers, and be a part of it as it goes on! There is so much to do. Too much to see. It's just a chill game once you've gotten past the main stuff. A lovely little endless road trip throughout one of the most artistically striking universes I have seen. And as of writing, no in-game NPC uses he/him. Extra points for the title.

I had gotten and played this game quite a while back on the game pass, but never went past a couple hours. Some while later I decided to give it a proper try, it seemed promising. But having played it now to its fullest, I don't understand fully the hype or the comeback people have writing out. I will just number of good and bad things, these are subjective but I think there is good feedback here, these are just things I consider foundational to a space-based game. [h2]Positives:[/h2] 1. Exploration is fun for a while and has depth, planets and animals are procedurally generated, so are tools. There are a fair amount of structures. 2. The storyline paired with its exploration and infinite universe mechanics is great, and really enjoyable. There's a lot of storyline content, a solid 60 hours (rough guess) if you don't cheese your way and go through it thoroughly. 3. You can build your own starship component by component, so that's quite fun and a nice part of the game. [h2]Negatives:[/h2] 1. Planets have no biomes, they are entirely one biome albeit all planets are different. 2. Animals are procedurally generated, but I think the library is lacking. Soon enough, after you explore a bit, you start seeing the similarities and how they are all built out of a few parts. 3. Structures are few and there's not much variation. The types of structures you can explore can be counted on your hands, there is no variation in their outer structures except space stations. 4. Space combat is bad, even on the highest difficulty, it would take you to use a laptop pad to control and possibly die. Worst of all, there is no strafing, so it can be frustrating dealing with space ships and structures sometimes. 5. Base designing is horrible. There are two kinds of structures in the game. The prebuilt fabs, and the ones which aren't prebuilt fabs (like individual pieces, you can use them for more specific designs, different material though). It becomes very apparent that prebuilt fabs are a later, more polished addition to the game because the other ones have horrible problems with them as they seem to have no snapping grids or such for in-structure technology and constructs (you have to literally eyeball everything, not to mention the build camera is clunky). Prebuilt fabs do have those building grids, making it easier to work with, but they can't be used to make somewhat specific exterior base designs. 6. Some foundational UI problems, the game was designed in mind with consoles and computers both. So they opted to use a UI which essentially both can use. But it's just annoying on a computer. I wish certain mechanics and parts of the UI were different for the computer, for example, you cannot take out a stack of item in the exact number you need, instead you need to repeatedly spam a button, separate it, then go back to the stack, and do it again. Custom waypoints in the galaxy map also don't work as they neither mark the waypoint, nor plot the route, so a bit buggy. Straight up annoying and unnecessary. 7. Difficulty settings don't scale up well, even on the hardest difficulty, the only annoying part is the item stack limit. Things can be cheesed through trade on every difficulty, including parts which are supposed to be hard to obtain. I would understand this on relaxed difficulty, but this needs to be curbed on higher sets. 8. Certain things don't really have a function whereas they seem they should. Like settlements, they serve zero function although you can commit a fair bit of time and resources to them, so they look nice, that's all. 9. They just launched the Swarm update, which brings in expedition 22, was my first expedition. It was exciting but then you hit a wall halfway, and it is time-gated and can only be progressed in after about 50 days save doing the same three repeatable boring missions every 8 hours. So, not a good look. 10. As fun as the story is, there is no post end game content loop. Once the missions are done, the game just feels empty. There is no automation, exploitation, sovereignty mechanics, basically any kind of engaging post end game loop. [h2]Opinion:[/h2] The game is fun till the storyline and missions are complete, which is a good amount of content, beyond that, there isn't much of anything. If you treat the game as a space sim with RPG content, you won't enjoy it. If you treat it as an RPG in a space sim, you will enjoy it. But with the way the sim is set and built, it just feels like wasted potential.

If you are someone who cares about quality and likes using your brain, do NOT buy this game. It was bad 10 years ago, and it is still bad today. Just less bad. My wife and I bought this game in hopes that 10 years of updates would overhaul all the negative press this game received upon coming out and trusted the general consensus of reviews claiming it is the "most improved" game of 2025-2026. While this game has massively improved, it has gone from a class action lawsuit of mis-advertising situation to -> present day: A very well polished turd! Despite fixing almost all the initial complaints from players, this game somehow manages to take every class in school and get a solid 50% F- in every class. No more, no less. You can tell there was a lot of thought and work behind the scenes to make this game playable and even have a whisper of 'fun' involved every 1 out of 100 hours. There just isn't a soul in this game when the exploration and mechanics are "as wide as an ocean and deep as a puddle" (yes that old adage still fits). Unfortunately, as a finely polished turd, they really shined this sucker up but nothing can mask that smell. I wanted SO badly for this game to be fun that I spent almost 400 hours 'giving it a shot'. I was disappointed 390 of those hours. I even beat the story twice and got every single achievement on Steam just to see if there is ANYTHING enjoyable on its own. I was devastated that there were no redeeming qualities. Unless this game is used as background noise or handed to a toddler as their first game ever played, I fail to see how this game is 'fun' to anyone. The 'Very positive' rating is just as 'procedurally generated' as the game itself. The advertising promises a space lover's dream, but is really just a purgatory of empty radiant tasks and lost potential. If you want to throw your head through your monitor in disappointment every time you get your hopes up that this quest isn't a complete waste of time, this game is for you! By all means, trust the positive reviews that only say "Spaaaace!" or "Yay, my dream game"... Or take the word of someone who toiled in misery so you wouldn't have to. You have been warned :).
